subject.title: fix(acp): add close() lifecycle method to SQLite event ledger

question: Which lifecycle boundary should own the ACP shared state DB cleanup for this bug: this PR's `AcpEventLedger.close()` contract, the narrower ACP server shutdown close shape, or the broader process-global cache lifecycle shape?
rationale: There are multiple open fixes for the same canonical issue, and this PR changes the internal ledger contract while sibling PRs keep cleanup at different owner layers; automation cannot safely choose the permanent boundary.

options.title: Prefer bounded server shutdown cleanup
options.body: Use the existing shared state DB close owner from ACP shutdown with a bounded drain or late-write gate, and avoid adding a ledger API unless maintainers explicitly need it.

options.title: Adopt the ledger close contract
options.body: Keep `AcpEventLedger.close()` as the explicit lifecycle seam, but require syntax repair, shutdown-order proof, test updates, and live shutdown evidence before merge.

options.title: Wait for process-global lifecycle ownership
options.body: Pause this PR while the broader state-cache lifecycle PR decides whether per-server cleanup should be replaced by owner-level exit handling.

recommendation.title: Prefer bounded server shutdown cleanup
recommendation.body: Use the existing shared state DB close owner from ACP shutdown with a bounded drain or late-write gate, and avoid adding a ledger API unless maintainers explicitly need it.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history makes steipete the strongest routing candidate for ACP/state lifecycle ownership among the likely owners.
